description:
Planning only. User requested this issue on 2026-11-20 while collecting more review comments. Do not start implementation until requested.

Problem
Delivery.Plan stores failure_policy while its TransportRequirements already stores the resolved policy. Normal planning copies the same value, creating two owners that can diverge.

Evidence and affected code
- lib/zaq/channels/delivery/plan.ex: struct field, typespec and restricted Inspect derivation.
- lib/zaq/channels/delivery/attachments.ex: normal plan constructor, requirements-error fallback, failure_notice, acquisition and preparation gates.
- lib/zaq/channels/delivery/executor.ex: validate_plan, run_uploads and run_publications.
- test/zaq/channels/delivery/executor_test.exs: synthetic plans currently omit requirements and set policy on Plan.
- test/zaq/channels/attachment_policy_test.exs: requirements-error test asserts plan.failure_policy.
- Inspect confirmation and Engine history Plan fixtures and active documentation for stale field references.

Required change
Remove the stored Plan.failure_policy field. TransportRequirements.failure_policy is the sole stored policy for attachment plans. Update all reads, constructors, types and Inspect derivation without exposing private plan data. Preserve selected-connector policy resolution; do not re-fetch or resolve settings during execution.

Fallback caveat
A blind replacement with plan.requirements.failure_policy is incorrect: requirements-error continue fallback and malformed-input notices currently construct requirements: nil plans with failure_policy: :continue. Preserve those text-only paths explicitly. Prefer one derived policy accessor shared by preparation and execution, with an explicit requirements-less continue case restricted to valid text-only fallback plans. Do not invent attachment limits or introduce another stored policy field. Reject malformed attachment-bearing plans before effects rather than silently defaulting to continue. Assess this proposed accessor against actual validation and fallback contracts before implementation.

Action reuse
Extend existing Plan/TransportRequirements and preparation/executor boundaries; local-only representation cleanup, no new Action, transport path or tool exposure.

Tests and invariants
Migrate executor fixtures to appropriate TransportRequirements with their policy. Update structural assertions to the retained owner while preserving existing behavioral scenarios. Preserve abort preparation/upload barriers and sequential publication; continue usable attachments, failure indices, root promotion and concurrency; requirements-error text fallback; malformed-input notice behavior; empty ordinary-text bypass; no retries; confirmation plan stripping. Cover invalid-plan handling before transport. Do not weaken tests or change supported delivery semantics.

Validation
Read AGENTS.md and applicable workflow, action-reuse, code-quality, documentation and testing policies. Recheck current workspace and preserve other agents' edits. Search source/tests/active docs for stale field references. Run affected preparation, executor, policy, API, Jido/SMTP and confirmation/history suites plus mix q per workflow. Final coverage/precommit remain zaq-1lw.13. No commit/push authorization. This issue blocks architecture review zaq-1lw.12.

Additional Plan/Step cleanup candidates (user review, 2026-11-20)
These extend this issue's review scope. Implementation remains on hold until requested; the attachment-reference item is conditional, not a demonstrated bug or blocker.

1. Remove repeated group.body from generated groups. Current generated groups copy outgoing.body, and publication_body already falls back to runtime.outgoing.body. Audit all producers and fixtures before removing reads/overrides; preserve failure-notice text, continuation captions and the notice-only canonical_body that retains the original answer. Do not remove canonical_body or notice?.

2. Move Step.prepared to runtime execution inputs. Generated planned steps leave it nil; execution populates an operation copy from runtime.prepared_steps. Keep prepared bytes/requests in execution-owned state and pass them through existing operation inputs to Jido/SMTP bridges. Update bridge consumers and fixtures together, without a parallel transport API or changes to materialization timing, authorization, acquisition count or preparation barriers. Remove the Step field/typespec only after all consumers are migrated.

3. Evaluate deriving publication Step.attachment_refs from its group. Send/edit steps currently repeat group membership, whereas upload steps require their own batch subsets. Simplify only if the existing executor contract can preserve original attachment indices, per-upload subsets, partial-success filtering, omitted groups, and effective references passed to bridges. Distinguish planned membership from the runtime successfully deliverable subset. If removal requires disproportionate branching or breaks supported synthetic/dependency plans, retain the field and document the reason rather than forcing deduplication.

Fields to retain
Keep Plan.placement as the chosen arrangement and requirements as the resolved constraints snapshot. Keep Step.id as stable opaque identity, operation as effective operation, and group_id as the relation: runtime promotion from send to edit can leave id unchanged, so do not derive operation from the id tuple. Keep message_ref as the approved existing target or earlier-result reference; do not rerun bridge eligibility against mutated executor outgoing data. Keep depends_on as explicit dependencies, upload attachment_refs as batch subsets, preparation_failures as reporting evidence, and notice metadata as distinct behavior controls.

Additional validation scope
Preserve existing behavioral coverage for ordinary and notice bodies, captions, original canonical text, runtime prepared transport requests, upload batching, partial failures, root promotion, existing-message edits and result dependencies. Update representation-only fixtures/assertions to their new owner; remove obsolete structural assertions only while retaining their behavioral coverage. Any change to existing behavioral expectations requires the repository's explicit approval gate. This issue update authorizes planning only, not code or test changes. Reuse existing preparation/executor/bridge operations; no new Action or transport path is warranted.

comments.text: Implementation authorized by user request 2026-11-20; representation-only test migrations explicitly authorized. Workspace initially clean at a6405a766. Plan: audit fallback/producer/consumer contracts; remove duplicated policy and body, move prepared into existing operation inputs; retain publication refs if dependency/subset semantics require them; validate affected suites and mix q. Action reuse: local-only extension of Plan/Attachments/Executor and existing Jido/SMTP execute_delivery_step operations; same inputs/outputs, trusted identity, effects, no retries or new Actions/tools. Policy snapshot stays selected-connector-owned; prepared payload lifetime stays executor-owned. Reject malformed attachment plans before acquisition/transport. Preserve stop barriers, continue concurrency/root promotion, notices/canonical body and confirmations. Roll back any candidate that changes supported behavior or requires weakening tests. E2E unnecessary for this behavior-preserving refactor; final coverage/precommit remain .13.

Implementation: removed Plan.failure_policy and copied group.body; Plan.failure_policy/1 derives from validated TransportRequirements or the exact single-send text fallback (no group/step refs, dependencies or message target, with failure evidence). Preparation and executor share it; invalid attachment-bearing plans fail before acquisition/effects. Removed Step.prepared; existing executor inputs.prepared carries runtime payloads to Jido upload and SMTP. Retained publication attachment_refs: executor unknown-text-only scenario deliberately uses empty step membership inside an attachment-bearing group; dependency/upload subsets and effective successful refs differ from group membership. Deriving these would change supported synthetic/dependency contracts or add branching. Kept canonical_body, notice?, placement, stable IDs, effective operation, message_ref, dependencies, failure evidence and upload subsets. Confirmation property migrated its private sentinel to opaque step identity while preserving Engine boundary stripping and immutability. Executor/history fixtures now provide resolved constraints. Focused executor/policy: 46 passed (7 properties), including new fallback, notice, runtime-payload and invalid-constraints coverage. Broader validation running. Context Mode transport is closed; logs redirected locally with bounded summaries; Serena Elixir navigation works.

Broad affected validation passed: 648 checks (21 properties, 627 tests), covering delivery preparation/executor/confirmation/error, attachment policy, API, Jido bridge and HTTP file delivery, SMTP/email outgoing attachments/sender/threading/collisions, Engine confirmation/history ingress and delivery, Agent attachment selection. Log: /tmp/zaq-1lw-28-affected.log. One background NodeRouter Channels API task logged DB sandbox owner exit after its test owner exited; ExUnit completed exit 0 with no failed checks. mix q initially caught one alias-style suggestion introduced in the policy assertion; corrected via the existing grouped alias. Final mix q passed (hooks, strict Credo, docs, compile/format), log /tmp/zaq-1lw-28-quality.log. Final focused rerun is checking the small plan_groups argument removal and formatted files. No commits/pushes; no dependency changes or unrelated workspace edits. Source/test/active-doc search found no stale plan.failure_policy, Step.prepared, step.prepared, group.body or group-body override reads. Final coverage/precommit remain .13; issue remains in progress pending review/landing per workflow.

Final validation complete: focused rerun against final formatted sources passed 123 checks (15 properties, 108 tests) in 7.7s; log /tmp/zaq-1lw-28-final-focused.log. Final mix q PASS and git diff --check PASS. Total broad run was 648 passed (21 properties); no test failures. Implementation complete in 11 scoped files, no commits/pushes. Candidate publication attachment_refs deliberately retained for distinct step subsets, successful upload references and supported synthetic dependency/text-only plans. No behavior expectations removed or weakened; representation-only property/fixture migrations were authorized by the user. Existing final review/coverage/precommit gates remain .12/.13.
